tagline: Pioneering accelerated computing to solve the world's most challenging computational problems
hero_kpi_rationale: Data Center revenue, driven by generative AI and Blackwell architectures, is NVIDIA's primary growth engine, representing the majority of its revenue and capturing the global wave of AI adoption.

kpis.name: Data Center Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Data Center segment powering AI and accelerated computing.
kpis.description: Data Center revenue increased 68% year-over-year, driven by demand for Blackwell platforms. It now represents the vast majority of total revenue.
kpis.signal: Massive growth driven by Blackwell and generative AI

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue remaining after deducting direct production costs.
kpis.description: Gross margin declined from 75.0% to 71.1% due to a $4.5B write-down on H20 inventory intended for China.
kpis.signal: High margin despite decline related to H20

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin reached 60.4%, supported by strong Data Center growth despite higher operating expenses.

kpis.name: R&D Investments (% revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: R&D expenses reached $17.5B in 2026, or 8.1% of revenue, reflecting continued commitment to technological innovation.
kpis.signal: R&D focused on AI innovation and new architectures

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Annual spending on physical and technological assets.
kpis.description: Capex of $6.1B in 2026 (vs $3.4B in 2025) includes investments in data center infrastructure, energy, and production capacity.
kpis.signal: Sharp increase in capex to support data center infrastructure

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Total headcount reached 26,300 employees, up 15%, supported by growth in Data Center and R&D operations.
kpis.signal: Strong headcount growth to support expansion

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Net profit after taxes, reflecting overall profitability.
kpis.description: Net income increased 65% to $120.1B in 2026, driven by strong Data Center demand.

kpis.name: H20 Revenue (China)
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the H20 product despite export restrictions.
kpis.description: Following a $4.5B inventory charge on H20, only $60M in revenue was generated in 2026 due to limited licenses granted by the USG.
kpis.signal: Marginal revenue from China due to regulatory restrictions

kpis.name: H20 Depreciation Charge
kpis.explanation: Accounting depreciation due to export restrictions on H20 chips.
kpis.description: In April 2025, the USG imposed an export license requirement for H20 to China, resulting in a $4.5B charge related to inventory overhang and purchase obligations.
kpis.signal: Major regulatory impact on quarterly results

kpis.name: Infrastructure Guarantees
kpis.explanation: Guarantees provided to support data center infrastructure deployment by partners.
kpis.description: NVIDIA provided $3.5B in site, energy, and building guarantees to early-stage companies, typically over multiple years.
kpis.signal: Strategic investment in the AI ecosystem

kpis.name: Venture Capital Investments
kpis.explanation: Investments in AI startups and infrastructure funds to support the ecosystem.
kpis.description: NVIDIA invested $17.5B in private companies and infrastructure funds, primarily to support early-stage startups purchasing its products directly or through cloud service providers.
kpis.signal: Massive commitment to the AI startup ecosystem

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury).
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + share buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

kpis.name: Data Center Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenu du segment Data Center qui alimente l'IA et le calcul accéléré.
kpis.description: Data Center revenue grew 68% year-on-year, fueled by demand for Blackwell platforms. It now represents the vast majority of total revenues.
kpis.signal: Massive growth driven by Blackwell and generative AI

kpis.name: Networking Revenue
kpis.explanation: $31 Mds en FY26, 10x vs FY21 (acquisition Mellanox). Spectrum-X + InfiniBand + NVLink. Q4 DC network
kpis.description: $31 Bn in FY26, 10x vs FY21 (Mellanox acquisition). Spectrum-X + InfiniBand + NVLink. Q4 DC networking up 142% YoY. Key to scaling out giga-AI factories.

kpis.name: Gaming Revenue
kpis.explanation: Q4 FY26 Gaming = $3.7 Mds (+47% YoY) via Blackwell GeForce. Annuel ~$13.5 Mds. Supply-constrained Q1
kpis.description: Q4 FY26 Gaming = $3.7 Bn (+47% YoY) driven by Blackwell GeForce. Annual run rate ~$13.5 Bn. Supply-constrained in Q1 FY27.

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: FCF FY26 = $97 Mds (Q4 seul $35 Mds). Retour actionnaires $41 Mds (43% FCF) en buybacks + dividendes
kpis.description: FCF FY26 = $97 Bn (Q4 alone $35 Bn). Shareholder returns of $41 Bn (43% of FCF) via buybacks and dividends.

kpis.name: Sovereign AI Revenue
kpis.explanation: Plus que triple YoY > $30 Mds. Nouveau vecteur de croissance (Europe, Moyen-Orient, Asie). Diversifi
kpis.description: More than tripled YoY to over $30 Bn. New growth vector (Europe, Middle East, Asia). Diversifies US hyperscaler concentration risk.

risks.title: Dependence on AI and accelerated computing demand
risks.score_rationale: Major risk positioned early in Item 1A (implicit in business structure). Intensive language on dependence on AI/HPC workloads. Growing trend with increased Data Center concentration. Very high categorical weight: >80% of revenue depends on accelerated computing demand.

risks.title: Increased competition from hyperscaler proprietary ASICs
risks.score_rationale: Critical business risk mentioned implicitly via NVLink Fusion strategy (FY2026) enabling custom CPU/XPU integration. Moderate language but strategically significant. Rising trend: Google TPU, Amazon Trainium/Inferentia, Meta MTIA represent growing threat. Very high categorical weight for business model sustainability.

risks.title: Extreme customer concentration with hyperscalers
risks.score_rationale: Specific business risk: text explicitly mentions 'all major public and private cloud providers' as direct customers. Intensive language on CSP dependence. Stable trend but structurally critical. Very high categorical weight: few customers represent >50% of Data Center revenue.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks and export restrictions (China)
risks.score_rationale: Business risk implicit in overall structure (Item 1C Cybersecurity mentioned). Moderate language but intense geopolitical context (US-China restrictions since 2023). Rising trend with new restrictions expected. High categorical weight: China historically represents ~20-25% of revenue.

risks.title: Critical dependence on CUDA and ecosystem fragmentation risk
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental business risk: CUDA described as 'foundational platform' and 'essential to modern computing'. Very intensive language on software ecosystem importance. Rising trend: competitors (AMD, Intel) investing heavily in alternatives (ROCm, oneAPI). Very high categorical weight for competitive moat.

risks.title: Manufacturing capacity and semiconductor supply chain
risks.score_rationale: Business risk implicit: NVIDIA depends on TSMC for fabrication (not explicitly mentioned but established). Moderate language on supply chain complexity (mention of 'extreme co-design'). Stable trend but structurally critical. High categorical weight: production bottleneck.

risks.title: Intellectual property and counterfeiting/piracy risks
risks.score_rationale: Specific business risk: text mentions 'inventions that are essential to modern computing' and IP importance (GPU, CUDA, Tensor Core). Moderate language. Stable trend but rapid growth context increases risks. Moderate categorical weight: IP protection critical for moat.

risks.title: Fast product cycles and technology obsolescence risk
risks.score_rationale: Business risk implicit: text mentions 'fast, yet harmonized, product and technology innovations' and accelerated cadence (Blackwell FY2025, Rubin FY2026, Blackwell Ultra FY2026). Moderate language but rising trend. Moderate categorical weight: rapid innovation is advantage but creates inventory depreciation risks.

ai_positioning.summary: NVIDIA is the undisputed leader in AI infrastructure, with technological dominance through its GPUs, CUDA ecosystem, and integrated data center platforms. Its Blackwell architecture has become the standard for AI training and inference.
evidence: Data Center revenue grew 68%, driven by Blackwell
Hundreds of thousands of interconnected GPUs forming AI supercomputers
Investments of $17.5B in AI startups and infrastructure funds
